slots.practicalActivity: Without touching a live system yet, sketch the request/response round trip for a plain-language scenario: LTV Manufacturing Corporation's expense system asking Oracle Fusion for a list of unpaid supplier invoices. Label the method, the resource, and what comes back, using only the vocabulary from this lesson.
slots.deliverable: One labeled sketch of a request/response round trip for the AP invoice scenario, naming the method, resource, and response in plain terms.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a reference card matching GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE to the status codes a Financials consultant actually sees (200, 201, 400, 401, 404), then hand-write a small valid JSON object representing one LTV Manufacturing Corporation supplier invoice (amount, currency, supplier, date), checking it for balanced braces and correct quoting.
slots.deliverable: A one-page HTTP method/status-code reference card plus one hand-written, syntactically valid JSON invoice object.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the real "REST API for Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials" documentation on docs.oracle.com and find the "Create an invoice" operation page. Identify its method, path, every required request-body field, and the response schema, then write out the minimal valid payload those required fields imply before you ever send a request.
slots.deliverable: A written minimal-required-fields payload for creating an invoice, built entirely from reading the real documentation page, with its five sections (method/path, params, body schema, response schema, example) each noted.

lessons.title: Oracle Fusion REST Resources for Financials
lessons.chapterTitle: Working with Oracle Fusion REST APIs

lessons.title: Making Your First GET Request
lessons.chapterTitle: Working with Oracle Fusion REST APIs

slots.practicalActivity: Against your Oracle Fusion practice environment, send a real GET request (via curl or Postman) to the invoices resource with Accept: application/json and limit=5, using Basic Authentication with an integration/test user. Inspect the real JSON response and identify the items array, count, hasMore, limit, and offset fields in the actual payload you received.
slots.deliverable: One successful real GET call to the invoices resource with its full JSON response saved, every top-level field (items, count, hasMore, limit, offset, links) labeled.

lessons.title: Querying, Filtering and Paging Results
lessons.chapterTitle: Working with Oracle Fusion REST APIs

slots.practicalActivity: Write and run a real q expression against the invoices resource for LTV Manufacturing Corporation retrieving unpaid invoices over $10,000 (q=InvoiceAmount>10000;InvoiceStatus='UNPAID'), then add fields= to restrict the response to just InvoiceNumber and InvoiceAmount, and finally page through the full result set using limit and offset until hasMore comes back false.
slots.deliverable: One documented q+fields query and a full paging trace (each limit/offset pair sent and each hasMore value received) through to the final page.

lessons.title: Creating and Updating Records
lessons.chapterTitle: Working with Oracle Fusion REST APIs

slots.practicalActivity: Send a real POST to the invoices collection URL creating one LTV Manufacturing Corporation supplier invoice with BusinessUnit, InvoiceCurrency, InvoiceDate, Supplier, and SupplierSite, capturing the new InvoiceId Fusion returns. Then send a PATCH to that specific invoice's own URL changing only its Description, and confirm every other field is untouched.
slots.deliverable: One newly created invoice (with its Fusion-assigned ID) plus one confirmed partial PATCH update that changed only the targeted field.

lessons.title: Working with a REST Client
lessons.chapterTitle: Working with Oracle Fusion REST APIs

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Postman (or Insomnia) collection for LTV Manufacturing Corporation's Fusion environment: set Basic Authentication once at the collection level, define {{base}} and {{v}} variables, then save the GET, POST, and PATCH requests from the previous three slots into it with clear names so a colleague could rerun every one without rebuilding them.
slots.deliverable: One saved REST client collection containing the GET, POST, and PATCH invoice requests, collection-level auth, and environment variables, each runnable without edits.

slots.practicalActivity: In your REST client, inspect the actual Authorization header your saved requests are sending under Basic Authentication, decode the base64 string by hand to confirm it reverses cleanly to username:password, and write out why that same header would instead carry a bearer token under OAuth 2.0 -- and why that matters for a user with MFA enabled.
slots.deliverable: A hand-decoded Basic Auth header showing the recovered username:password, plus a written comparison of what the header would carry (and why) under OAuth 2.0.

slots.practicalActivity: Design a least-privilege integration user for LTV Manufacturing Corporation's AP bank-feed integration (e.g. integration.ap.bankfeed), naming its specific job/duty roles, business unit scope, and read-vs-write access, instead of reusing a personal login. Then deliberately send one malformed request to trigger a real 400 error, read its title/status/detail/o:errorCode shape, and write the correct retry logic (no retry) versus what you'd do for a 429 or 503 instead.
slots.deliverable: One documented least-privilege integration-user design plus one captured real error response with a written retry-or-not decision and justification.

slots.practicalActivity: For four real LTV Manufacturing Corporation scenarios -- a one-time 50,000-row legacy journal conversion, a vendor portal invoice arriving now, a nightly AR aging extract to a collections tool, and 'notify finance the moment a large journal posts' -- classify each by pattern (batch/bulk, real-time REST, event-driven) and direction (inbound/outbound), justifying each with the volume/latency/direction/frequency questions from the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A four-scenario classification table naming pattern and direction for each, each justified against the lesson's four deciding questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram how Oracle Integration Cloud's ERP Cloud adapter would subscribe to a Payables 'invoice created' business event for LTV Manufacturing Corporation once Enable Business Events is set for that module, contrasting it against a polling integration that calls GET /invoices?q=CreationDate>... every 15 minutes -- labeling exactly where the delay and the wasted calls disappear in the event-driven version.
slots.deliverable: One side-by-side polling-vs-event-driven diagram for the same invoice-created scenario, with delay and call-volume differences explicitly labeled.

lessons.title: Exchanging Financial Data with External Applications

slots.practicalActivity: Course capstone lab: a client asks for a new integration pulling AR aging data into a collections tool every morning. Without being told the answer, write a full requirements summary the way a Financials consultant actually would -- the resource(s) involved, direction, likely pattern, and at least four specific field mappings between Fusion's attribute names and the collections tool's fields -- using only this course's own vocabulary and tools (REST client, documentation, auth, patterns) with no code written.
slots.deliverable: A complete written integration-requirements summary for the AR-aging-to-collections scenario: resources, direction, pattern, and at least four named field mappings.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can read Oracle Fusion's REST API documentation, make real authenticated GET/POST/PATCH calls against Financials resources with a REST client, choose the right authentication and integration-user design, and scope requirements for a real Fusion integration using the correct pattern (batch, real-time, or event-driven).
